dependencyChain: Charge side for reference: POST /orders -> placeOrder -> chargeCard -> provider.charge; placeOrder -> query (INSERT INTO orders, stores charge_id)
keyFindings.criticalNote: No refund flow is wired up. No API route exists for refunds (api-routes.js has only /login, POST /orders, GET /reports/sales, DELETE /admin/users/:id), and refundCharge in payments.js has no callers. Also, refundCharge swallows provider errors and always returns true, so a failed refund would look successful. Nothing in the database layer handles refunds, and no refund status is stored; the orders table only records charge_id.
keyFindings.summary: The codebase has no end-to-end refund flow from API to database. The only refund code is refundCharge(chargeId) in payments.js, which calls provider.refund and is never called from anywhere, and the API routes expose no refund endpoint.

keyFindings.module: External integrations and their error handling
dependencyChain: auth.js login -> query; login -> jwt.sign / verifyToken -> jwt.verify (jsonwebtoken)
api-routes.js (express) -> requireUser -> verifyToken; POST /orders -> placeOrder -> chargeCard
keyFindings.criticalNote: Payment refunds and email failures are silently swallowed: refundCharge catches provider errors with an empty catch and always returns true, and sendOrderEmail has an empty catch. Also, the route handlers have no error handling, and requireUser never gets a null token check (verifyToken returns null instead of throwing, so req.user is null and req.user.id throws later).
keyFindings.summary: External dependencies are the npm packages express, pg, and jsonwebtoken, plus node:crypto (built-in), along with two stub modules, provider-stub.js (payment provider) and mailer-stub.js (email). Neither stub file appears in the file listing, so those imports cannot resolve as the code stands. Error handling is inconsistent: the database and auth layers let errors propagate or return null, while payments and email swallow failures, and the express routes have no try/catch or error middleware.

dependencyChain: placeOrder -> reserveStock (inventory.js), called in a loop over cart.items
placeOrder -> query: INSERT INTO orders (user_id, total, charge_id) RETURNING id (database.js: pool.connect -> connection.query -> connection.release)
keyFindings.criticalNote: The database is reached only after stock reservation and card charging have already run. placeOrder loops with i <= cart.items.length, so cart.items[length] is undefined and reading .sku throws on the last iteration, before cartTotal, chargeCard, or the INSERT run. If the INSERT fails after chargeCard succeeds, the customer is charged with no order row. Also, query() never releases the connection when connection.query throws, which leaks pool clients.
keyFindings.summary: POST /orders runs requireUser, then placeOrder, which reserves stock, computes the total, charges the card, and inserts the order row through query() in database.js. The reserve loop has an off-by-one bug that throws before any charge or insert happens. The route has no try/catch, so a thrown error reaches Express without a JSON response.
